sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This suit is filed by the deceased plaintiff for the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction to restrain the defendants or any persons claiming on behalf of them from interfering with her peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule site bearing No.286/A1 situated at Rajmahal Vilas,
2 nd Stage layout (Old Geddalahalli), Bangalore.

During the pendency of the suit, plaintiff -Dr.M.
Leelavathi died and her son is brought on record as her legal representative and he has prosecuted the suit.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as hereunder:-
The Bangalore Development Authority has acquired various lands at Geddalahalli village and formed sites.

The suit schedule site being one of such site is allotted to the plaintiff by BDA by executing a registered lease-cum-sale agreement dated 08.02.2011 and delivered the vacant physical possession of the suit schedule property through the possession certificate dated 08.02.2011.

The plaintiff being a senior citizen served in Kannada Film Industry for more than 55 years as an artist, carried good reputation in the society and as she had no property at Bengaluru, the BDA has allotted the site to her.

After securing the possession, she had constructed a shed in the suit site and drilled borewell and covered the suit schedule property by putting up compound wall by spending more than 5 lakhs and appointed a watchman who is residing in it along with his family members in the existing shed.

On 02.05.2012,
some unknown persons visited the suit schedule property and attempted to dispossess the plaintiff from it and after lodging the complaint, the plaintiff came to know that those people are the persons sent by the defendants in the guise of the order obtained by the defendants in W.P.No.8566-67/2011 challenging the acquisition of lands and claimed possession.

But, as against the order passed in the Leelavathi M vs Rama Murthy M on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122602544/
2 aforesaid writ petition, the BDA has preferred Writ Appeal No.842-843/2012, which is pending before the Hon'ble High Court.

sentences.text:
The plaintiff being an allottee having purchased the suit schedule property and khatha having been entered in her name pursuant to the allotment order the defendants have no right to interfere with her possession over the suit schedule property and as there is an order by the Hon'ble High Court in W.P.No.8566- 67/2011, the police have advised her to approach the court and therefore, to protect her possession,
she has approached this court seeking the above reliefs.
3. Pursuant to the suit summons issued by this Court, the defendants entered appearance and filed their written statement.
In the written statement, the defendants have denied the right, title, interest and possession derived to the plaintiff through the allotment order made by BDA.

It is contended by the defendants that their grand-mother one Smt.Akkayamma had purchased 17 guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Geddalahalli village along with 6 guntas of phot kharab through a registered sale deed dated 12.04.1932 and was in possession of the same.

Subsequently, Smt.Akkayamma executed a WILL dated 01.12.1980 bequeathing it in favour of defendant No.1 and thereafter, the defendants have been enjoying it as its absolute owners and in possession by changing the khatha in their name.

The acquisition proceedings made by BDA is challenged by the defendants by filing W.P.No.8566-67/2011 against BDA as well as the plaintiff, which came to be allowed by the Hon'ble High Court and the entire acquisition proceedings are quashed holding that the acquisition proceedings are illegal.

Therefore, the allotment order made in favour of the plaintiff and also lease-cum- sale agreement executed in favour of the plaintiff dated 08.02.2011 do not confer any right to the plaintiff and the possession was also continued with the defendants.
It is contended that the plaintiff has attempted to dispossess the defendants from the suit schedule property and therefore, a complaint also came to be lodged on 21.03.2012.

It is further contended that if the plaintiff had paid the sale consideration, her remedy is only to approach the BDA for re-allotment of any other alternative site or refund the amount from BDA and she cannot claim right or possession over the suit schedule site.

In the additional written statement filed by defendants, they have specifically denied the possession of the plaintiff and contended that the defendants and predecessors in title have been in possession of the suit schedule property from time immemorial and therefore, suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Court has framed the following issues:-
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of suit?
2) Whether the plaintiff further proves the alleged interference of defendants?
3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief's claimed?
4) What decree or order?

 REASONS  8. Issue No.1:-

The plaintiff has pleaded that the deceased plaintiff Smt.Leelavathi was a senior citizen served in Kannada Film Industry for more than 55 years as an Artist and carried good reputation in the society and she was even honoured by awarding Kannada Rajyotsava award and considering her service, the BDA had allotted the suit schedule site bearing No.286/A1 at Rajmahal Vilas, 2nd Stage Layout under G-category through an allotment order dated 03.02.2011 and lease-cum-sale agreement dated 08.02.2011 was executed and the possession is also delivered to her through the possession certificate dated 08.02.2011 and thereafter she came into possession of the suit schedule property, constructed a shed in it, drilled a Borewell, built compound wall, appointed watchman, availed electricity connection and while in possession of the site on 02.05.2012, the defendants interfered over her possession and therefore filed this suit to protect her possession over the suit schedule property.

On the other hand, the contention of the defendants is that originally the suit schedule property along with the larger extent measuring 17 guntas and 6 guntas of phot kharab was purchased by the grand-mother of the defendant no.1 Smt.Akkayyamma through a registered sale deed dated 12.04.1932 and thereafter she had executed a WILL dated 01.12.1980 through which the defendant no.1 came into possession and enjoyment of the property.

It is their contention that though the BDA had acquired it by a notification, the same is challenged by them by filing Writ Petition No.8566-67/2011, which came to be allowed and the allotment order is cancelled.

The possession claimed by the plaintiff over the suit schedule site is disputed by the defendants and they have contended that they have continued in possession of the property, and the plaintiff herself has interfered over their possession.

Per contra,
the plaintiff has contended that though the acquisition notification was quashed and allotment order was cancelled as against the order, BDA has preferred Writ Appeal before the Hon'ble High Court by filing Writ Appeal No.842-843/2012 in which the Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court has directed status-quo as regards, possession and title.

sentences.text: The plaintiff during the course of evidence disputed the title of the defendants over the suit schedule site.

But, the defendants have produced RTC pertaining to 23 guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Geddalahalli Village at Ex.D2, which indicates that it was initially acquired by Akkayyamma and thereafter the defendants have succeeded to the property.

Though it is contended on behalf of the plaintiff that the land acquired is Sy.No.5 and not in sy.no.4, it is brought on record that earlier there was a house constructed by the defendants in the disputed property, which is demolished by the BDA for which the Hon'ble High Court has directed the BDA to pay compensation to the defendants.

Therefore, the identity of the property and question of title is not much significant more particularly when the writ petition filed by the defendants challenging the acquisition notification is allowed by the Hon'ble High Court and as they were directed to pay compensation for the demolition of the building by BDA.

10. As observed above, the plaintiff is claiming right and possession over the suit schedule site on the basis of the allotment order made by BDA as per Ex.P1 allotment letter, lease-cum-sale agreement produced at Ex.P3 and possession certificate issued as per Ex.P5.

But, in the Writ Petition No.8566- 67/2011 filed by the defendants against BDA and the plaintiff Dr. Leelavathi along with other writ petitions, the acquisition of the property from the defendants and allotment of sites was the subject matter before the Hon'ble High Court.
The Hon'ble High Court in the writ petition after elaborate discussion quashed the allotment order made by BDA in favour of the plaintiff Dr Leelavathi.
Though the said order is challenged by BDA, it is admitted fact that the plaintiff has not challenged the order dated 02.09.2011 passed in WP No.8566-67/2011.
It is true that in the written appeal, the Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court has directed to maintain status-quo in respect of possession and title.
But, the quashing of land acquisition proceedings as well as the allotment order made in favour of the plaintiff by BDA is not stayed by the Hon'ble Division Bench.

Therefore, for all practical purposes, this court is required to take note that both the acquisition of the land by BDA and allotment of site in favour of the plaintiff are cancelled by the Hon'ble High Court as per the order dated 02.09.2011.
Though the Writ Appeal is pending it is well settled position that mere pendency of appeal will not operate as stay.

11. In the course of judgment passed in the writ petition filed by the defendants, the Hon'ble High Court has made some important observations in respect of the process of acquisition as well as taking possession of the property.

The Hon'ble High Court in para No.57 of the judgment has observed that in the total extent of 1331 acres of land declared for the purpose of implementation of the scheme in question, only 629 acres of land had been handed over to the Engineering section of BDA and the remaining acquired land is not utilised.
In para No.63 of the judgement, the Hon'ble High Court has disbelieved process of taking possession by BDA in respect of the lands notified.

In para No.66, the Hon'ble High Court has observed that the demolition of the buildings in the acquired lands are illegal and therefore BDA shall pay compensation to the land owners including to the defendants.
Ultimately, in para No.76, the Hon'ble High Court has quashed the allotment orders.

In this regard, the specific observations made by the Hon'ble High Court in para Nos.57, 63,
66 and 76 of W.P.No.8566-67/2011 and connected cases is extracted for ready reference:-
"57.

This version as claimed by and presented before this Court and is accepted without further scrutiny, but only shows that BDA has utilized an extent of 380 acres Leelavathi M vs Rama Murthy M on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122602544/

63. Firstly, the original record, particularly, the award and the spot mahazar on which reliance is placed for issue of the notification under section 16[2] of the BDA Act and paragraphs 8, 9 and 10 of the award passed in respect of this land very clearly shows the most inconsistent and irreconcilable narration as noticed in paragraphs 8,
9 and 10 of the award and to crown the illegality or irregularity the spot mahazar does not contain the signature of any witnesses but is only a self serving spot mahazar containing signatures of officials of the BDA, but not one single independent witnesses having witnessed taking possession of the land.

If such is the spot mahazar evidencing taking of possession which alone can result in the land vesting in the State Government and in turn to be handed over and with the assertion of the petitioners that they have never been disturbed from their possession hitherto and they have been put in possession by their erstwhile vendors etc., their version cannot be brushed aside as even durable possession of the land by petitioners being conceded and intention of the BDA to take possession as of now, the notification under section 16[2] of the BDA Act and presumptive value as per this provision are all of no consequence even as noticed in GOKULA EDUCATION FOUNDATION's case [supra)
and the very original records having betrayed the authority and not making good taking possession of the subject land, the assertion of the petitioners that the possession had remained with them, not much importance needs to be attached to the defence put up by the BDA about the presumption under section 16[2] of the Act and is therefore rejected but other consequences as above do follow....

66. Insofar as claim towards compensation claimed by some of the writ petitioners due to demolition of their buildings in the subject land are concerned, this court had passed interim order directing the BDA to pay an adhoc amount.
It is the submission of Mr.Bhagwat, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that this amount is also not paid.
However, Sri Shankaranarayana Rao, learned counsel for the BDA submits that this is also appealed against.
76. It is therefore these writ petitions are allowed.
The impugned notices and allotment are quashed by issue of writ of certiorari".
The above observations made by the Hon'ble High Court indicate that the BDA itself had not taken possession of the notified properties including the suit schedule site in accordance with law.

Therefore, when there is no material on record to show that BDA had taken possession of the property, question of delivering the possession to the plaintiff by way of possession certificate produced at Ex.P5
cannot be accepted.

The quashing of land acquisition notification goes to the root of the matter and upsets the entire process of allotment of site in favour of the plaintiff including the execution of lease-cum-sale agreement.

sentences.text: The defendants have also seriously disputed the existence and identity of suit schedule site claimed by the plaintiff.
The suit schedule site is described as site No.286/A1.
In this regard the defendants have produced the layout plan at Ex.D6.This
site No.286/A1 do not find place in Ex.D6 layout plan.
This is confirmed by BDA by issuing a confirmation letter as per Ex.D5 when the defendant No.1 has sought the information under Right to Information Act.
Learned counsel appearing for plaintiff by relying upon the office note of AEE, North Division, R.T. Nagar has contended that appropriate amendment process is under progress.
Needless to mention that the layout plan prepared by BDA shall be approved by the Government.
Admittedly, the suit schedule site finds place in the approved layout plan nor the layout plan is amended to recongnise the suit schedule site.
This is more important for the reason that the plaintiff is relying upon the delivery of possession of suit schedule site from BDA, which do not find place in the layout plan.

In order to grant an order of injunction, the description of the property is very much relevant and when the suit schedule site is not found in the approved layout plan of BDA, it is improper to pass a decree in respect of a site number, which is not in existence in the approved layout plan.

13. Learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff strongly contended that the construction of the shed,
drilling of the borewell, putting up of compound wall, appointment of watchman, availing of the electricity connection are the clear proof of the settled possession of the plaintiff over the suit schedule site.

He has also contended that in a suit for bare injunction, the question of title is insignificant and therefore, when there are materials on record to show that the plaintiff is in settled the possession of the property, the plaintiff cannot be dispossessed without following due process of law and therefore, the plaintiff is entitled for protection.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff, a person who is in settled possession of the property cannot be dispossessed without following due process of law even by a true owner.

As rightly pointed by the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff the customer history statement pertaining to the electricity connection availed indicates that temporary electricity connection was availed by the plaintiff on 05.03.2011 itself which is evident from Ex.P62 statement.
The subsequent receipts and electricity bills produced before the court show that the electricity connection was continued.

But,
there is no evidence to show that when exactly the shed was put up or borewell was drilled and compound wall was constructed.

Though the photographs produced by the plaintiff indicates the existence of a compound wall, shed and a borewell, the evidence prima- facie indicates that they were put up hurriedly and they are temporary structures.

It appears that on the basis of the allotment letter made by BDA, the plaintiff has entered the suit site and put a temporary shed consisting of sheets, a raw compound wall and borewell was also drilled and temporary electricity connection is availed.
The point for consideration is whether this possession claimed by the plaintiff is matured to the status of settled possession.
It is well settled law that a casual act of possession without continuous and sufficiently long period cannot be construed as a settled possession.
Insofar as cultivable lands are concerned, if the person who is in possession of the property cultivates and grown-up crops, such possession will be treated as settled possession.
Admittedly, in the present case, the plaintiffs are not residing in the suit schedule site.
It is true that a temporary shed is constructed, a compound wall came to be put up and a watchman is appointed to look after the site.
On the basis of the above facts, the court is required to consider whether the possession claimed by the plaintiff is the settled possession.

In this regard, in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Ramegowda (dead) by LRs v/s Varadappa Naidu (dead) by (2004)1 SCC 769,

sentences.text: 7 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that mere stray or intermittent acts of trespass do not partake the character of settled possession and in order to mature the possession as a settled possession, it should be a sufficiently long period and the possession should be matured.

In this regard, in para No.9 & 10 of the judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as hereunder:-
"It is the settled possession or effective possession of a person without title which would entitle him to protect his possession even as against the true owner.
The concept of settled possession and the right of the possessor to protect his possession against the owner has come to be settled by a catena of decisions.
Illustratively, we may refer to Munshi Ram v. Delhi Admn., Puran Singh v. State of Punjab and Ram Rattan v. State of U.P.

entities.text: Puran Singh v. State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ram Rattan v. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The authorities need not be multiplied.

In Munshi Ram case, it was held that no one, including the true owner, has a right to dispossess the trespasser by force if the trespasser is in settled possession of the land and in such a case unless he is evicted in the due course of law, he is entitled to defend his possession even against the rightful owner.
But merely stray or even intermittent acts of trespass do not give such a right against the true owner.

The possession which a trespasser is entitled to defend against the rightful owner must be settled possession,
extending over a sufficiently long period of time and acquiesced to by the true owner.
A casual act of possession would not have the effect of interrupting the possession of the rightful owner.
The rightful owner may re-enter and reinstate himself provided he does not use more force than is necessary.
Such entry will be viewed only as resistance to an intrusion upon his possession which has never been lost.
A stray act of trespass, or a possession which has not matured into settled possession, can be obstructed or removed by the true owner even by using necessary force.
In Puran Singh case the Court clarified that it is difficult to lay down any hard-and-fast rule as to when the possession of a trespasser can mature into settled possession.
The "settled possession" must be (i) effective, (ii) undisturbed, and (iii) to the knowledge of the owner or without any attempt at concealment by the trespasser.
An occupation of the property by a person as an agent or a servant acting at the instance of the owner will not amount to actual physical possession.

The nature of possession of the trespasser would,
however, be a matter to be decided on the facts and circumstances of each case;

8 (iii) the process of dispossession of the true owner by the trespasser must be complete and final and must be acquiesced to by the true owner; and (iv) that one of the usual tests to determine the quality of settled possession, in the case of culturable land, would be whether or not the trespasser, after having taken possession, had grown any crop.

sentences.text: If the crop had been grown by the trespasser, then even the true owner, has no right to destroy the crop grown by the trespasser and take forcible possession.

10. In the cases of Munshi Ram and Puran Singh the Court has approved the statement of law made in Horam v. R. wherein a distinction was drawn between the trespasser in the process of acquiring possession and the trespasser who had already accomplished or completed his possession wherein the true owner may be treated to have acquiesced in; while the former can be obstructed and turned out by the true owner even by using reasonable force, the latter may be dispossessed by the true owner only by having recourse to the due process of law for reacquiring possession over his property".

14. In view of the above legal position, though there is evidence to show that the electricity connection was obtained on 05.03.2011, there is no clear evidence as to when this compound wall and shed were put up in the suit schedule property.
The allotment letter was issued on 03.02.2011.
But, the defendants have challenged the acquisition notification as well as allotment of site immediately thereafter on 24.02.2011 by filing WP No.8566- 67/2011.
In other words, before availing the electricity connection by the plaintiff on 05.03.2011, the defendants have challenged the very allotment order on 24.02.2011.

It indicates that when the matter was subjudiced before the Hon'ble High Court later which was allowed by the Hon'ble High Court, the plaintiff has taken steps to assert possession over the suit schedule property.

Therefore, when an allotment order was made and probably before entering of the plaintiff to the suit schedule property, the defendants have challenged the action of allotment of BDA by filing the aforesaid writ petition wherein ultimately they have succeeded and the allotment order itself is cancelled.

15. At the cost of repetition, it is important to point out that the very basis of flow of possession to the plaintiff through the allotment letter dated 03.02.2011 is quashed by the Hon'ble High Court.
The acquisition of the land is also quashed.
Admittedly, the deceased plaintiff or his son are not residing in the suit schedule property.

Therefore, it is not proper to hold that the plaintiff is in settled possession of the schedule property merely on the basis of the temporary shed and compound wall put up in the suit schedule property, which is made subsequent to the filing of the writ petition.
16. It is also necessary to note that the relief of injunction is an equitable and discretionary relief.
This is specifically provided under section 36 of the Specific Relief Act 1963.
Therefore, the discretion should be exercised judiciously.

When the Hon'ble High Court has elaborately dealt with the writ petition filed by the defendants against the plaintiff and quashed the allotment order, it is not judicious to grant the relief of injunction, even if the court holds that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule property.
Therefore, issue No.1 is answered in the negative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
In view of the answer given to issue No.1 in the negative, question of interference by the defendants does not arise.
Further, the defendants have succeeded in W.P.No.8566-67/2011 and therefore the claim made by the defendants cannot be considered as a wrongful interference.
Hence issue No.2 is answered in the negative.
18. Issue No.3 & 4:-
In view of the answer given to issue No.1 & 2 in the negative, the plaintiff is not entitled for any relief in the present suit.

The court recognizes the service rendered by the deceased plaintiff Dr.M.Leelavathi as a versatile and a talented actress who paved the way for many woman in Kannada Film Industry and her contributions are even recognized with several awards including the National Film Awards, Karnataka State Film awards.

Unfortunately, BDA has allotted a site, which do not find place in the approved layout plan and made the plaintiff/s to litigate to get her right after payment of huge amount as consideration for the site.
It appears that she has spent money even after the allotment.
In view of the answer given to issue No.1 & 2 as above, though the court cannot grant any relief in favour of the plaintiff, the suit cannot be said to be false or frivolous.
The plaintiff has come before the court on the basis of the allotment order made in her favour.
Therefore, it is not proper to direct the plaintiff to pay cost while dismissing the suit.
19. The court believes and hopes that alternative suitable site will be allotted by BDA to the plaintiff/s to protect their interest.

When the Government and BDA has already taken up a decision that the plaintiff is entitled for a site under G-category, it is the obligation of the BDA to allot alternative suitable site befitting to the status of the plaintiffs for which they have already paid the amount.
On these observations, the issue No.3 is answered in the negative and the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is dismissed.
However, Court believes and hopes that BDA will allot suitable alternative site to the plaintiff's considering their contribution to the Karnataka Film Industry.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff being a senior citizen served in Kannada Film Industry for more than 55 years as an artist, carried good reputation in the society and as she had no property at Bengaluru, the BDA has allotted the site to her.
On 02.05.2012,
some unknown persons visited the suit schedule property and attempted to dispossess the plaintiff from it and after lodging the complaint, the plaintiff came to know that those people are the persons sent by the defendants in the guise of the order obtained by the defendants in W.P.No.8566-67/2011 challenging the acquisition of lands and claimed possession.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Court has framed the following issues:-
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of suit?
2) Whether the plaintiff further proves the alleged interference of defendants?
3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief's claimed?
4) What decree or order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But, the quashing of land acquisition proceedings as well as the allotment order made in favour of the plaintiff by BDA is not stayed by the Hon'ble Division Bench.
Therefore, when there is no material on record to show that BDA had taken possession of the property, question of delivering the possession to the plaintiff by way of possession certificate produced at Ex.P5
The quashing of land acquisition notification goes to the root of the matter and upsets the entire process of allotment of site in favour of the plaintiff including the execution of lease-cum-sale agreement.
But,
there is no evidence to show that when exactly the shed was put up or borewell was drilled and compound wall was constructed.
Though the photographs produced by the plaintiff indicates the existence of a compound wall, shed and a borewell, the evidence prima- facie indicates that they were put up hurriedly and they are temporary structures.
It is well settled law that a casual act of possession without continuous and sufficiently long period cannot be construed as a settled possession.
Insofar as cultivable lands are concerned, if the person who is in possession of the property cultivates and grown-up crops, such possession will be treated as settled possession.
Admittedly, in the present case, the plaintiffs are not residing in the suit schedule site.
It is true that a temporary shed is constructed, a compound wall came to be put up and a watchman is appointed to look after the site.
In this regard, in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Ramegowda (dead) by LRs v/s Varadappa Naidu (dead) by (2004)1 SCC 769,
Leelavathi M vs Rama Murthy M on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122602544/
The allotment letter was issued on 03.02.2011.
But, the defendants have challenged the acquisition notification as well as allotment of site immediately thereafter on 24.02.2011 by filing WP No.8566- 67/2011.
It indicates that when the matter was subjudiced before the Hon'ble High Court later which was allowed by the Hon'ble High Court, the plaintiff has taken steps to assert possession over the suit schedule property.
Therefore, when an allotment order was made and probably before entering of the plaintiff to the suit schedule property, the defendants have challenged the action of allotment of BDA by filing the aforesaid writ petition wherein ultimately they have succeeded and the allotment order itself is cancelled.
Therefore, it is not proper to hold that the plaintiff is in settled possession of the schedule property merely on the basis of the temporary shed and compound wall put up in the suit schedule property, which is made subsequent to the filing of the writ petition.
Therefore, the discretion should be exercised judiciously.
When the Hon'ble High Court has elaborately dealt with the writ petition filed by the defendants against the plaintiff and quashed the allotment order, it is not judicious to grant the relief of injunction, even if the court holds that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff has come before the court on the basis of the allotment order made in her favour.
Therefore, it is not proper to direct the plaintiff to pay cost while dismissing the suit.
When the Government and BDA has already taken up a decision that the plaintiff is entitled for a site under G-category, it is the obligation of the BDA to allot alternative suitable site befitting to the status of the plaintiffs for which they have already paid the amount.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In order to grant an order of injunction, the description of the property is very much relevant and when the suit schedule site is not found in the approved layout plan of BDA, it is improper to pass a decree in respect of a site number, which is not in existence in the approved layout plan.
The subsequent receipts and electricity bills produced before the court show that the electricity connection was continued.
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. The court believes and hopes that alternative suitable site will be allotted by BDA to the plaintiff/s to protect their interest.
On these observations, the issue No.3 is answered in the negative and the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is dismissed.
However, Court believes and hopes that BDA will allot suitable alternative site to the plaintiff's considering their contribution to the Karnataka Film Industry.
Draw decree accordingly.
